entry.name: Machine Learning Specialization
entry.note: Andrew Ng's rebuilt classic; the most common starting point in the field

covers: Supervised learning: linear and logistic regression
Model evaluation and best practices for generalisation
Decision trees, random forests and boosted trees
reading.format: Three courses. Each lesson gives a visual explanation of the concept first, then a code walkthrough, with the underlying math in optional videos. The material includes practice quizzes, graded assignments and practice labs, and the work is done in Python rather than Octave.
reading.summary: The Machine Learning Specialization is a beginner-level program of three courses made by DeepLearning.AI with Stanford Online and taught by Andrew Ng. It is a rebuilt and expanded version of Andrew Ng's earlier machine learning course, with assignments and lectures moved to Python. Learners build and train models in Python using NumPy, scikit-learn and TensorFlow, starting from linear and logistic regression and going on to neural networks, tree ensembles, clustering, recommender systems and reinforcement learning. Finishing it shows the learner can build learning algorithms and apply them to real applications.
reading.audience: People starting out in AI who want a foundation in machine learning. The page says no prior math knowledge or rigorous coding background is needed, and that it also suits those who began the original course without finishing it or who want to refresh their foundations.
reading.prerequisites: None stated. The page says the program does not require prior math knowledge or a rigorous coding background.
